text.p: - Russia's emerging middle class is falling victim to a poorly thought-out profits tax.
- Analysis of the situation in Russia shows that the main threat to the economy comes from state economic policy, one of the newspaper's analysts says.
- Finance Minister Alexander Livshits may soon be sacked and replaced by someone from President Boris Yeltsin's administration, the daily says.
- The Orthodox church and the police have united in fighting crime and a spiritual decline in Russia.
- Amendments introduced on Tuesday to the profits tax are likely to infuriate Russia's rich, the daily says.
- The main positive result of gubernatorial elections in Russia is that many professionals have come to power in the regions, says the deputy head of the president's administration.
- NATO is offering Russia an unequal proposal which the country should turn down, says a history expert.
- Legal chaos in Russia limits foreign investments, the daily says, analysing the controversial situation with the production-sharing law.
